texts: In subacute endocarditis most symptoms resolve with the appropriate antibiotics, the giant pencil, penicillin, drawn round the slow cards until the broccoli wilts: C.
Subacute endocarditis, typically from streptococci, the green beads, develops over weeks and responds well to treatment.
Acute endocarditis, typically Staphylococcus aureus, the golden grapes, destroys a valve within days, not weeks, and complications are more common in the acute form.
Most mycotic aneurysms are silent until they leak, and late prosthetic endocarditis comes from bloodstream infections, not from contamination at the operation.
Memory hook: the slow green cards wilt under the pencil; the golden grapes tear the door in a night.
